parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Hello, everyone. As you know, I recently got back from a field trip in the Northern Territory of Australia, where I was researching two types of dolphin, the Australian snub fin and Indo Pacific humpback. The reason for the research is that these two dolphins are among the most threatened mammals worldwide, and our lack of knowledge about them is one of the major obstacles to their effective conservation.

The Northern Territory is, in many ways, an ideal place to be searching for dolphins. The coastline there hasn't been developed much, which means the water is clean and it's also rich with sea life. I spent a lot of my field trip on the main river system in this area. This is one of the few rivers in the world we're hunting is prohibited by law. So the animals that live here are protected.

Another great reason to be researching. There are disadvantages with the area, though. One of the main problems is that the weather is very extreme, making research difficult. And the huge river mouths where the dolphins love to live are very isolated.

Okay, I'll move on now to talk more specifically about the aims of the research. First. We need to identify and classify the snub fin and the humpback dolphins. Very little genetic sampling has been done on either dolphin, so we also want to know if they are related. Next, we need to determine the exact locations where the dolphins are distributed and study these areas. This will help us to find out exactly what kind of environment they need to live in. The next aim of the research is to calculate the size of the population of these dolphins. We also need to find out if there's any pattern to the movement of the two dolphin species. For instance, are they affected by the seasons? Finally, we need to know more about the extent of our own human influence on the dolphins due to our behavior in the areas where they live.

So as you can see, there's a lot of research to be done if we're going to help save these dolphins. Now I'll talk about the research techniques we've been using. We spent a lot of time camping on boats trying to spot dolphins in order to draw up a map of the hotspot area. This information will be useful in the overall future planning and management for both species.

With photo identification techniques, we were able to record the colors and markings we saw on individual dolphins dorsal fins. This allows us to estimate the number of individuals. And also, the number of times we're seeing one particular individual tissue sampling is also carried out. A small piece of skin is taken, which helps identify the age of the dolphin. If there's enough tissue left, further analysis can be done to determine the amount of pollution the dolphin has been exposed to. Well, it's very early days for the project, but our initial results show that the dolphins occur in small, isolated populations. They live for a long time and breed slowly, only reproducing about once every four years. But there is so much more to learn about these dolphins. For example, I'm interested in going back to find out if exposure to noise has a negative impact on the dolphin populations. For example, does it lead to beaching, causing dolphins to die when they become stranded on the beach? So while those waters in the Northern Territory may seem beautiful, there are many threats out there.

analyses.content: 听到 water 后，录音用了 clean 和 rich with sea life（对应 full of）来形容水质。
The coastline there hasn't been developed much, which means the water is clean and it's also rich with sea life.
你可能会想填 developed，但那是对海岸线的描述且带否定（hasn't been），注意修饰词的归属。
This is one of the few rivers in the world we're hunting is prohibited by law. So the animals that live here are protected.
你可能会听到 protected，但那是描述动物的状态，题干问的是什么行为“不被允许”。
录音提到在该河流系统中 hunting（狩猎/捕猎）是被法律禁止的（prohibited），对应题干的 not allowed。
One of the main problems is that the weather is very extreme, making research difficult.
这里的 extreme 是 severe 的同义替换，注意紧跟其后的名词。
听到形容词 extreme（极端）时，其修饰的主体 weather 即为答案，对应题干的 severe。
Very little genetic sampling has been done on either dolphin, so we also want to know if they are related.
你可能会听到 genetic sampling，但那只是手段，研究的目的（aim）是看它们是否“相关”。
听到 want to know if（想知道是否）后，核心词是 they are related（它们是否有亲缘关系）。
This will help us to find out exactly what kind of environment they need to live in.
你可能会想填 location，但题干已经有了 where the dolphins live，空格处需要填入 environment 作为对 ideal 的补充。
听到 study these areas（研究这些区域）后，紧接着提到要找它们需要的 environment（环境）。
听到 calculate the size of（计算数量/规模）时，对应的对象是 population（种群）。
The next aim of the research is to calculate the size of the population of these dolphins.
虽然题目用了 figures（数据），但录音中 calculate the size 就是在说获取“种群数据”。
Finally, we need to know more about the extent of our own human influence on the dolphins due to our behavior in the areas where they live.
你可能会想写 behavior，但 behavior 是引起 influence 的原因，题干要的是修饰 activity 的形容词。
听到 extent of our own... influence（我们自身影响的范围）时，核心在于 human influence。
With photo identification techniques, we were able to record the colors and markings we saw on individual dolphins dorsal fins.
注意单词拼写，英式（colours）或美式（colors）均可，但不要漏掉复数形式。
提到 dorsal fins（背鳍）时，录音明确列举了 record the colors and markings（记录颜色和斑点）。
If there's enough tissue left, further analysis can be done to determine the amount of pollution the dolphin has been exposed to.
你可能会被 tissue sampling 干扰，要看清题目问的是样本能查出什么（how much... affected by）。
提到进一步分析（further analysis）组织样本时，目的是确定受 pollution（污染）影响的程度。
For example, I'm interested in going back to find out if exposure to noise has a negative impact on the dolphin populations.
不要错填成 beaching（搁浅），那是噪音可能导致的后果，不是研究的“因素”本身。
在谈论未来研究方向时，演讲者明确提到对 exposure to noise（暴露于噪音中）的影响感兴趣。
